goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Adding the same normalized host with a different category succeeds, but imports select the first mapping and silently publish into the earlier category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue: the EmbeddableHost model has no uniqueness validation on the 'host' field (line 2 only validates format). The record_for_host method (lines 10-17) uses `.first` to select a host record, meaning if duplicate hosts exist with different categories, only the first one is used for topic creation. In topic_embed.rb lines 36-37, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` is called and its category_id is used. This means adding the same host twice with different categories would succeed (no uniqueness constraint), but imports would silently use the first category found, which is unexpected behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Deleting the existing `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site-setting keys breaks settings-API clients that still read or write them.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that deleting site settings breaks 'settings-API clients'. However, this is a migration that is part of a deliberate refactoring to move embeddable hosts from site settings to a dedicated database table. The migration properly migrates existing data before deleting the old settings. This is intentional behavior change, not a bug. External API clients that depend on internal site settings are not a supported use case, and the change is a valid architectural decision to use a proper database model instead of site settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Host entries containing an accepted port never match URI.host, so saving example.com:8080 still leaves embedding denied.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/embeddable_host.rb, the before_validation callback strips the protocol and path from the host (lines 5-7), but the validation regex on line 2 explicitly allows ports: `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`. So a host like 'example.com:8080' can be saved. However, in the `record_for_host` method (lines 9-17), it extracts `uri.host` which returns just the hostname without the port (e.g., 'example.com'), then compares it against the stored host value which includes the port ('example.com:8080'). This means the comparison `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` will never match when a port is stored, causing embedding to be denied even for valid hosts with ports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Limiting the top-level domain to five letters rejects valid hosts such as example.technology and prevents configuring their embedding relationships.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters, which would reject valid modern TLDs like .technology, .photography, .international, etc. This is a real bug that prevents legitimate hosts from being configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The category lookup returns no row for the default blank `embed_category`, so dereferencing `[0]['id']` aborts migration before the fallback can preserve any embedding configuration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, lines 10-14 show: the query joins categories with site_settings where s.value = c.name AND s.name = 'embed_category'. If embed_category is blank/empty (the default), this query returns no rows. Then line 11 tries to access `[0]['id']` on an empty result set, which would cause a nil/error before reaching the fallback on lines 14-16. The finding correctly identifies that dereferencing [0]['id'] on an empty result will fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Copying legacy URL/path host-list entries verbatim bypasses normalization, so entries such as `http://discourse.org` no longer match the new hostname-only lookup and existing embeds are rejected after deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 copies legacy embeddable_hosts entries verbatim with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. However, the EmbeddableHost model has a before_validation callback that strips 'http://' and 'https://' prefixes and trailing paths. Since the migration uses raw SQL INSERT, it bypasses this normalization. Meanwhile, the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host method extracts just the hostname from URLs and does a case-insensitive lookup. If legacy entries contain 'http://discourse.org', they won't match lookups for 'discourse.org', breaking existing embeds after migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — force: true` drops an existing `embeddable_hosts` table during migration, risking irreversible loss of already-provisioned relationship data.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that `force: true` risks data loss of 'already-provisioned relationship data'. However, this is a NEW migration creating a NEW table (`embeddable_hosts`) that didn't exist before. The `force: true` option would only drop the table if it already exists, but since this is the initial creation of this table as part of a feature migration, there would be no existing data to lose. The migration is actually migrating data FROM the old `site_settings` table (embeddable_hosts setting) INTO this new table structure. This is not a bug - it's a standard migration pattern for creating new tables.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — The irreversible raw deletion of both legacy settings has no `down` restoration, so a rollback cannot recover the host/category configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb uses `def change` but contains irreversible operations - specifically `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` on line 31. This deletion cannot be automatically reversed by Rails, and there's no `down` method to restore the data. While this is a valid concern about migration reversibility (making rollbacks impossible without data loss), it's not a bug per se - the migration will work correctly going forward. It's an architectural/operational concern about the inability to rollback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — saveChanges` has no caller, leaving a misleading unused update path for future maintainers.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims `saveChanges` has no caller and is unused. However, looking at the diff, `saveChanges` is an action defined in the controller that would be called from the template via Ember's action helper. While the embedding.hbs template shown in the diff doesn't explicitly show a button calling `saveChanges`, this is a standard Ember pattern where actions are wired up in templates. The action exists to handle saving embedding settings, and the template may call it through a button not fully shown, or it may be intended for future use. The finding incorrectly assumes the action is dead code when it's actually a standard controller action pattern in Ember.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Each public embed request performs an uncached, unindexed case-insensitive host lookup, adding a table scan and database round trip at traffic scale.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host method performs a database query with 'where("lower(host) = ?", host)' on every embed request. Looking at the diff, there's no index added in the migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb only creates the table with host and category_id columns, no indexes). The case-insensitive lookup using lower() would prevent index usage even if one existed. This is a legitimate performance concern for a method called on every embed request (used in embed_controller.rb's ensure_embeddable and topic_retriever.rb). However, this is not a bug per se - it's a performance/scalability concern that's valid but may not matter at small scale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — A failed delete rejects without a handler, leaving the administrator without failure feedback and producing an unhandled async error.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff at app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6 lines 42-48, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but there is no `.catch()` handler. In contrast, the save action at lines 35-39 properly handles errors with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the delete operation fails (network error, server error, etc.), the promise rejection will be unhandled, leaving the user without feedback about the failure. This is a real defect in error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — Updates and deletes dereference a missing record, so a stale request after concurrent deletion returns a 500 instead of a recoverable not-found response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, the update and destroy methods use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` which returns nil if the record doesn't exist. In the update method, `save_host(host)` would be called with nil, causing a NoMethodError when trying to call `host.host = ...`. In the destroy method, `host.destroy` would similarly fail with NoMethodError on nil. This is a real bug - there's no nil check or proper 404 handling for missing records.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The migration dereferences the first embed-category override row before checking for its absence, so upgrades fail on sites that retain the default unset setting.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code at line 11: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c...`)[0]['id'].to_i`. If the query returns no rows (when embed_category setting doesn't exist or doesn't match any category name), then `[0]` returns `nil`, and calling `['id']` on `nil` will raise a NoMethodError. The check `if category_id == 0` on line 14 happens after the potential nil dereference, not before. This is a real bug that would cause migrations to fail on sites without the embed_category setting configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Unescaped legacy host values are interpolated into SQL, so a URL path containing an apostrophe breaks the upgrade and crafted stored values can alter the statement.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 25 uses string interpolation to insert the host value directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The host values come from the old site_settings table and are not sanitized. If any host value contains a single quote (apostrophe), it would break the SQL syntax. More seriously, if malicious data was stored in the embeddable_hosts setting, it could lead to SQL injection during the migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — The new spec only asserts class inheritance, so create, update, delete, category fallback, and validation-error behavior can regress without detection.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new spec file at spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb only tests class inheritance ('is a subclass of AdminController'). Looking at the diff, the controller at app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb has create, update, destroy actions with specific logic including category_id fallback to uncategorized_category_id, validation error handling, and save operations. None of this behavior is tested by the minimal spec. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5 — The embedding endpoint spec only asserts inheritance, leaving the serialized and sorted host relationship that supplies the admin UI unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new embedding_controller_spec.rb only tests inheritance (line 5-7: 'it "is a subclass of AdminController"'). The diff shows the EmbeddingController has a show action that serializes embeddable_hosts with ordering (EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)), but there's no test verifying this serialization or ordering behavior. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality, though the controller logic is relatively simple.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:25 — The new client save, cancel, and delete flows have no test coverage, so category edits and failed saves can regress silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new client-side component code in embeddable-host.js.es6 with save, cancel, and delete actions that handle category editing, error handling via popupAjaxError, and state management. Looking at the test files added (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb), they only contain minimal tests checking class inheritance. There are no JavaScript tests for the new embeddable-host component. The finding correctly identifies that this new nontrivial client-side logic lacks test coverage, which is a legitimate review concern for newly added functionality.
